meta.triageRationale: One story with one obvious approach: read two optional keys from the global config and pass them to the existing update paths. Three source files and their tests, one module family, no storage or contract change.

override.reason: Owner approved the LLD with an override; the three review findings (single-branch clone refspec, check order, single-branch fixtures) are recorded as binding requirements in docs/plans/daemon-update-source.md.

summary.prose: The daemon update takes its git remote URL and branch from two optional keys in ~/.insrc/config.json (daemonUpdate.repoUrl and daemonUpdate.branch), so a fork or a feature branch can be deployed. One validated reader serves the daemon.update IPC helper and the CLI update; the helper script gets a --repo-url flag, and a switch to another branch is a clean checkout of origin/<branch>. Empty or absent keys leave today's behaviour unchanged.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Make the daemon update source (repo URL and branch) configurable

api.name: readUpdateSource

parameters.name: configPath
parameters.purpose: the config file to read; defaults to PATHS.config

returns.meaning: { repoUrl?: string; branch?: string } with only the keys that are set and valid; an absent file or empty keys give {}

errors.condition: the file is not valid JSON, daemonUpdate is not an object, or a value is not a string or fails validation (a URL that starts with '-', has whitespace or control characters, or is not an https, ssh, git or file URL, an scp-style git@host:path, or an absolute path; a branch outside the conservative ref pattern, containing '..', '//', a trailing '/' or '.lock')

postconditions: a returned repoUrl and branch are safe to pass as single git arguments

api.name: launchUpdate

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: test seams; gains readSource for the config reader

errors.condition: 'daemon.update: invalid daemonUpdate config: <reason>' when the reader throws; nothing is spawned and no marker is written

postconditions: the detached helper is spawned with `<daemonCtl> restart [--repo-url <url>] [--branch <name>]`, a flag present only for a key that is set

api.name: runDetachedUpdate
api.signature: function runDetachedUpdate(daemonCtl: string, deps?: UpdateRunnerDeps, subcommand?: string, extraArgs?: readonly string[]): Promise<DaemonUpdateOutcome>
postconditions: extraArgs reach daemon-ctl.sh after the subcommand; the detached entry takes them from argv[4..]

api.name: update
api.signature: function update(opts: UpdateOptions, onLog: LogFn): Promise<MaintenanceResult>

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: gains repoUrl?: string; branch keeps winning over the config

errors.condition: 'invalid daemonUpdate config: <reason>'; 'working tree has uncommitted changes' or 'HEAD has commits no remote branch has' when switching branch or remote; 'HEAD diverged from origin/<branch>' as today

postconditions: with no repoUrl and no branch configured the sequence is the one that ran before this Story

api.name: daemon-ctl.sh --repo-url

parameters.name: --repo-url
parameters.purpose: the remote origin must point at before the fetch

returns.meaning: 0 success; 3 for a dirty tree, local-only commits or a diverged HEAD; 1 for a malformed flag

errors.condition: --repo-url without a value, or a value that starts with '-'

postconditions: origin's URL equals --repo-url when given (set with `git remote set-url origin`, logged)
when --branch differs from the current branch the checkout is `git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>` after the tree and local-commit checks

dataModelChanges.details: Two optional string keys: daemonUpdate.repoUrl and daemonUpdate.branch. Empty string or absent means 'keep the checkout as it is'. Both get CONFIG_CATALOG rows (group General, default empty string) so the settings list shows them and the boot reconcile keeps them.
repoUrl?: string, beside the existing branch?: string; both override the config when given.
readSource?: () => UpdateSource, the config reader seam.

errorCases.scenario: The config has an invalid value (a URL that starts with '-' or has whitespace, a branch with '..', a non-string, or daemonUpdate that is not an object)
errorCases.detection: readUpdateSource validates each value and throws UpdateSourceError naming the key and the reason
errorCases.response: launchUpdate throws 'daemon.update: invalid daemonUpdate config: <reason>' before anything is spawned; the CLI update returns { ok: false, error } before the first git command
errorCases.userImpact: The update does not start and the message says which key to fix

errorCases.response: UpdateSourceError 'config.json cannot be read as JSON' and the same refusals as above
errorCases.userImpact: The update refuses rather than running against the checkout's current branch with a config nobody could read

errorCases.scenario: The working tree has uncommitted changes when the branch or remote is being switched
errorCases.detection: the existing `git diff --quiet` and `diff --cached` checks in sync_repo, and `git status --porcelain` in maintenance.ts
errorCases.response: exit 3 'uncommitted local changes; refusing to overwrite'; the remote URL is not changed before this check
errorCases.userImpact: Nothing is switched; the person commits or discards the changes

errorCases.scenario: HEAD has commits that no remote branch contains and the branch is being switched
errorCases.detection: `git branch -r --contains HEAD` prints nothing after the fetch
errorCases.response: exit 3 'HEAD has commits no remote branch has; refusing to switch'
errorCases.userImpact: Local work in the daemon checkout is never discarded by a checkout -B

errorCases.scenario: The fetch fails (the URL is wrong, the branch does not exist there, or the network is down)
errorCases.response: the script dies with the fetch error (set -e); the CLI returns 'git fetch origin/<branch> failed'; origin's URL stays as set so a later run retries
errorCases.userImpact: The daemon keeps running the code it has; the outcome record says the update failed

errorCases.scenario: The fork's branch has diverged from the checkout's HEAD while the branch name is unchanged
errorCases.detection: merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/<branch> fails, as it does today
errorCases.response: exit 3 'HEAD has diverged from origin/<branch>; resolve manually'
errorCases.userImpact: A person re-clones or resets the checkout; the message says so

edgeCases.input: Neither key is set, or both are empty strings
edgeCases.expected: readUpdateSource returns {}; no flag is passed; no remote or branch is touched
no `set-url` is run and nothing is logged for it

edgeCases.input: branch equals the current branch and repoUrl is unset
edgeCases.expected: the sequence that ran before this Story: fetch, ff-only merge

edgeCases.input: branch names a branch that does not exist locally but exists at origin
edgeCases.expected: `git checkout -B <branch> origin/<branch>` creates it from the fetched ref

edgeCases.input: repoUrl is an absolute local path or a file:// URL
edgeCases.expected: accepted, so a fork can be tried from disk and the script test can use a temporary remote

edgeCases.input: opts.branch is given to the CLI update and the config also names a branch
edgeCases.expected: opts.branch wins; the config's repoUrl still applies

invariantsToPreserve.text: The update refuses a dirty tree and a diverged HEAD instead of overwriting; this Story adds checks and never removes one
The IPC update spawns a detached helper that outlives the daemon and writes an outcome record; a launch failure writes no marker and spawns nothing
The CLI update never starts the daemon and runs the config reconcile and steering refresh after the build
Config keys the catalog declares are filled by the reconcile and keys it does not know are left alone, so an empty default means 'unset'

testLevels.purpose: The config reader and the launcher's argument building, with injected seams and no git or daemon

update-runner.test.ts: launchUpdate passes --repo-url and --branch only for the keys that are set, and an invalid config spawns nothing and writes no marker
fixturesNeeded: the existing spawn, lock and clock seams in update-runner.test.ts

testLevels.purpose: The real daemon-ctl.sh sequence against a temporary git remote and checkout, with --skip-install and --skip-build
subjects: daemon-ctl-source.test.ts: daemon-ctl.sh update with --repo-url and --branch points origin at the URL, switches to the branch and fast-forwards, and refuses a dirty tree and local-only commits
maintenance-source.test.ts: the CLI update applies the configured repo URL and branch the same way, and opts.branch wins over the config
fixturesNeeded: a temporary bare remote and clone created with git in the test

migration.stateBefore: The daemon update always syncs the installed checkout against origin and the branch the checkout has checked out (daemon-ctl.sh sync_repo with BRANCH defaulting to HEAD's branch; maintenance.ts update with opts.branch defaulting the same way). The daemon.update IPC passes no flags, and no setting names a remote URL or a branch.
migration.stateAfter: Two optional config keys, daemonUpdate.repoUrl and daemonUpdate.branch, name the remote and branch the update follows. The IPC helper and the CLI update read them through one validated reader; daemon-ctl.sh accepts --repo-url; a switch to another branch is a clean checkout of origin/<branch>. With the keys empty or absent the behaviour is the one before.

migrationSteps.action: Add the two catalog rows with empty-string defaults; the next boot reconcile writes them into config.json as empty strings, which mean unset
Ship the reader, the launcher and CLI changes and the new script flag; nothing changes until a key is set
The owner sets daemonUpdate.branch (and repoUrl for a fork) in config.json; the next update switches the checkout

migration.backwardCompat: No public API changes. The script keeps every existing flag and its exit codes; --repo-url is additive. UpdateOptions and UpdateRunnerDeps gain optional fields. An older daemon that does not know the keys ignores them, and the reconcile of an older build leaves unknown keys alone.

alternativesConsidered.name: One TypeScript reader, flags to the script
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A small module reads `daemonUpdate.repoUrl` and `daemonUpdate.branch` from the global config; the IPC helper passes them to daemon-ctl.sh as --repo-url/--branch, and maintenance.ts uses them directly.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add src/shared/update-source.ts with readUpdateSource(configPath?) returning { repoUrl?, branch? } after validating each value. update-runner.ts reads it when it spawns the helper and appends --repo-url and --branch to the daemon-ctl.sh arguments. daemon-ctl.sh gains --repo-url: before the fetch it runs `git remote set-url origin <url>` when origin differs, and when the wanted branch differs from HEAD it checks it out (creating it from origin/<branch>) after the dirty check. maintenance.ts update() applies the same steps through its capture/stream helpers, with opts.branch winning over the config. Unset keys change nothing.
pros: The config is parsed and validated in one place that both TypeScript paths share
The script keeps flags only, so it stays usable by hand and has no JSON parser
Reuses the existing --branch flag and UpdateOptions.branch
cons: The set-url, checkout and fetch sequence exists twice, in the script and in maintenance.ts, as the sync logic already does
A new flag on the script

alternativesConsidered.name: Environment variables only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: daemon-ctl.sh and maintenance.ts read INSRC_DAEMON_REPO_URL and INSRC_DAEMON_BRANCH; the config is mapped onto them by the launcher.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The script and maintenance.ts read the two environment variables; update-runner.ts copies the config values into the helper's environment. No new script flags.
pros: No flag parsing change in the script
A fork can also be selected for one run from the shell
cons: Two places to set the same thing, and the TUI path would also need the mapping
Environment values are easy to leave set by accident and are not validated at the boundary the way a config reader would
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Works, but the values reach the script through the environment unvalidated and the TUI path still needs its own mapping, so it duplicates more than a1.

alternativesConsidered.name: The script reads the config itself
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: daemon-ctl.sh parses ~/.insrc/config.json with node and applies the repo URL and branch; maintenance.ts shells out to it or repeats the parse.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a small node one-liner in the script to read daemonUpdate.repoUrl and daemonUpdate.branch, validate them in shell, then run the same set-url, checkout and fetch steps. maintenance.ts would call the script's update command instead of its own sequence.
pros: The script alone knows the source, so a hand run and the IPC run agree
One implementation of the sequence if maintenance.ts delegates
cons: Replaces the CLI's own sequence, which also runs the config reconcile and steering refresh between the build and the end, so it is a larger change than the Story asks
Validation of a URL in shell is weaker than in TypeScript
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Moves parsing into shell and would replace the CLI sequence that also runs the config reconcile and steering refresh; larger than the Story asks.
